ops.text: (d) Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, losses, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or the Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of any applicable law, rule or regulation; (iii) any unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company's Confidential Information or data caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give Contractor prompt written notice of the claim, and Contractor shall have control of the defense and settlement of the claim (provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or admission on Company shall be made without Company's prior written consent), with Company's reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense. Contractor's obligations under this Section 7(d), and Company's recovery in respect of them, shall not be subject to the limitation of liability in Section 7(a). Company shall indemnify Contractor only against third-party claims to the extent arising out of materials or content furnished by Company to Contractor or Company's breach of applicable law.

quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Section 7's heading promises indemnification, but the section contains only liability provisions: 7(a) mutual fee-based caps, 7(b) consequential damages waiver, and 7(c) an attorneys' fees waiver. A full-text search for "indemnif" returns only the heading, and "hold harmless" returns nothing, so no operative indemnity of any kind exists in the agreement. Section 5(c) gives a bare non-infringement warranty on the Works but no defence or indemnity obligation, and the warranty is in any event capped at fees paid under 7(a) (whose carve-out points to Paragraph 9, which is the Independent Contractor clause — an apparent mis-reference to a deleted indemnity section). Absence of any Vendor IP indemnity is walk-away territory under this rule and fails both the preferred and fallback positions, so we have inserted a Contractor indemnity as new Section 7(d) covering third-party IP infringement, breach of law, data/Confidential Information breach and gross negligence or wilful misconduct, with standard notice/control/cooperation mechanics, a carve-out from the 7(a) cap, and a reciprocal Company indemnity narrowed to Company-furnished materials and Company's breach of law. The heading is conformed to remove the one-sided "OF CONTRACTOR" reference. We flagged the cap carve-out here only because the indemnity is newly inserted; the adequacy of the 7(a) cap itself is a separate limitation-of-liability issue.

Section 7(b) does give a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages, and the Company-side cap at fees paid is favourable to us and left untouched. quote: Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services")
rationale: The Agreement imposes no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation on Clear Capital, which matches the playbook's preferred position. Engagement is structured "on a task by task basis" under separately negotiated Statements of Work (p0004), the term is open-ended and terminable under Paragraph 6 (p0011), and compensation is per-SOW time and materials with no minimum volume, requirements commitment, or sole-source condition (p0013). Targeted searches for "exclusive", "sole supplier/provider/source", "all of its requirements", "exclusivity" and "shall not procure ... from any third party" surfaced no restriction on our freedom to buy elsewhere. The apparent gap at section 2 in the outline is cosmetic: "2. TERM" sits at p0011 within sec-1 and contains no scope or exclusivity language, so absence is confirmed rather than assumed. The three "exclusive" hits are unrelated and none binds our purchasing freedom: Contractor's retained ownership of its pre-existing property (p0020), a royalty-free non-exclusive license granted to us (p0021, which benefits Customer), and the entire-agreement clause (p0051). The mutual non-solicitation of employees at p0047 is a personnel restriction rather than exclusive dealing and is addressed under a different rule, so it is not double-flagged here. This clause set meets the preferred position outright; no fallback reliance and no redline are required.

quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
rationale: The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, stipulated damages, penalty, kill-fee or minimum-fee-on-termination obligation payable by Clear Capital. Termination under § 6(a) (convenience, 15 days' notice with no outstanding SOW) and § 6(b) (material breach), and the duplicate wind-down provision at § 7(c) (p0044), obligate us only to pay fees and expenses actually incurred or earned through the effective date of termination — that is payment for work performed, not a liquidated amount or early-termination fee. § 3 (p0013–p0015) sets time-and-materials compensation, expense reimbursement and taxes, with no late-payment penalty or interest charge; § 7 (p0035–p0037) caps each party's liability at fees paid to Contractor and excludes consequential damages, with no penalty or liquidated-damages carve-out from the cap. Accordingly the document sits at the preferred position (no liquidated damages or penalties payable by Customer) and no redline is warranted. Noted only for completeness (not deviations under this rule): Contractor may change rates on 30 days' notice (p0014), which is a pricing point rather than a liquidated amount.

quote: (c) To the extent that Contractor incorporates any of Contractor's Information into the Works, Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: This clause sits at the fallback and is therefore compliant; no redline is proposed. The only licence in our favour is § 4(c) (p0021). Material term 1 - not revocable at will: the grant is expressly "perpetual", carries no "revocable" qualifier, and there is no discretionary revocation hook anywhere; § 6(a) and § 6(b) (p0032, p0033) terminate the Agreement and Statements of Work but are silent on revoking this licence, and § 4(d) and § 7(c) confirm our continuing right to modify the delivered software after termination or final payment. The walk-away scenario (licence revocable at Vendor's discretion) is absent. Material term 2 - affiliates and contractors: the word "Affiliates" does not appear, but the express "right to grant a sublicense", read with the broad permitted purpose "in connection with Company's business operations", is a workable path to extend the licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf. That defeats the walk-away test ("affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them") and reaches the fallback ("affiliates covered on written notice") in substance; the absent keyword is a phrasing variant, not a coverage gap. Material term 3 - successor transfer: the general non-assignment clause (p0042) requires the other party's consent but provides it "will not be unreasonably withheld", a practical route to a successor in an M&A transaction - again at the fallback rather than the preferred position. Shortfalls against the preferred wording are minor sub-elements noted here rather than flagged: no express "irrevocable", affiliates and contractors not named in the grant, and no explicit M&A carve-out from the assignment consent. Under the playbook's classification semantics a clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined, so flagging would be over-flagging. If § 4 or § 10 is reopened for other reasons, the low-cost asks are adding "irrevocable", inserting "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", and carving M&A successors out of the p0042 consent requirement.

quote: 13. NON-SOLICITATION OF EMPLOYEES. Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

There is no restrictive-covenant section (outline: §§ 1-7), and searches for competing products/business, exclusivity, "engage in" and "Company shall not" turn up nothing of the kind. The only party-facing covenants are (i) § 13 (p0047), a mutual, reciprocal 12-month employee non-solicitation, which restricts hiring of personnel rather than the businesses we may operate or the products we may buy or build, and (ii) p0020, a limitation on reselling or reusing Contractor's own pre-existing proprietary materials outside the software we receive — an ordinary IP licence-scope limit, not a restriction on our competitive activity. This meets the preferred position (no non-compete or field-of-use restriction on Customer), so no redline is warranted under this rule.
